description:
Send a calendar event invitation.

Set exactly one recipient: `number`, `group_id`, or `contact_id`.

`start_at` and `end_at` are ISO 8601 **with an offset**, for example
`2026-09-10T14:00:00Z`. A timestamp without one is rejected: the
recipient's phone renders the event in their own timezone, so an
ambiguous instant would show the wrong hour on their screen.

When set, `end_at` must be after `start_at`; an event that ends before
(or exactly when) it starts is rejected.

`location` pins where it happens (`latitude` and `longitude`, with an
optional `name` and `address`). `has_reminder` reminds guests, and
`reminder_offset_sec` says how many seconds before the event;
`extra_guests_allowed` lets guests bring extra people.

To fix a mistake later (a typo, the description, a link), use
`edit_calendar_event`: guests keep their answer. When the date, time or
place change and guests must accept again, cancel the event with
`cancel_calendar_event` and send a new one with this tool. The
entry a guest added to their own calendar with the card's "Add to
calendar" button never follows an edit or a cancel: it stays on the old
date and adding again creates a second entry, so tell guests to delete
the old one. To see who said they are coming, use `get_message_responses`.

EventLocation.description: Where a calendar event takes place: a map pin with an optional name and address.

address.description: The place's address, up to 500 characters.
address.title: Address

name.description: A name for the place, up to 200 characters.
name.title: Name

url.description: A link shown beside the pin.
url.title: Url

EventLocation.title: EventLocation

contact_id.description: Recipient contact id (`ct_…`), from `list_contacts`. A contact id belongs to one number: an id from one inbox does not address the same person in another. Set exactly one of `number`, `group_id` or `contact_id`.
contact_id.title: Contact Id

description.description: Details shown on the event, up to 2000 characters.
description.title: Description

end_at.description: When the event ends. ISO 8601 with an offset, and later than `start_at`.
end_at.title: End At

extra_guests_allowed.description: Set to true to let guests bring extra people. Off when left out.
extra_guests_allowed.title: Extra Guests Allowed

group_id.description: Recipient group id (`grp_…`), from `list_groups`. A group id belongs to one number: an id from one inbox does not address the same group in another. Set exactly one of `number`, `group_id` or `contact_id`. Addressing a group needs a plan that includes group messaging: without it the call answers `payment_required: feature_not_available`, and retrying will not change that.
group_id.title: Group Id

has_reminder.description: Set to true to remind guests before the event. Off when left out.
has_reminder.title: Has Reminder

idempotency_key.description: Any printable ASCII text you choose, 1 to 255 characters, for example the id of the event you are answering. Reusing it for the same number suppresses a duplicate if you retry. Without it, retrying after a timeout may deliver the message twice, and the recipient sees both.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

join_link.description: A link guests can open to join, for example a video call.
join_link.title: Join Link

location.description: Where the event takes place: a map pin with an optional name and address.

name.description: The event's title, up to 200 characters.
name.title: Name

number.description: Recipient phone number in E.164 form, digits only, country code first (e.g. `5511999999999`). Set exactly one of `number`, `group_id` or `contact_id`.
number.title: Number

number_alias.description: Which of the organization's WhatsApp numbers this acts on: `main`, the alias of an extra number, or the number's `id` (`num_…`), which stays the same when the alias is renamed. Call `list_numbers` to see them. Defaults to the main number.
number_alias.title: Number Alias

quoted_message_id.description: Quote an earlier message (`msg_…`) so it appears above yours. Do this only when your text depends on something said a while ago, yours or theirs; do not quote the message you are answering right now, send a normal message instead.
quoted_message_id.title: Quoted Message Id

reminder_offset_sec.description: How many seconds before the event the reminder goes off, for example 600 for ten minutes. Only takes effect together with `has_reminder`.
reminder_offset_sec.title: Reminder Offset Sec

start_at.description: When the event starts. ISO 8601 with an offset, for example `2026-09-10T14:00:00Z`. A time without an offset is rejected.
start_at.title: Start At

name: send_calendar_event
title: Send a calendar event
